title: RobustSpring: Benchmarking Robustness to Image Corruptions for Optical Flow, Scene Flow and Stereo
claim: A benchmark systematically covers many corruption categories, applied consistently across time, stereo and depth, for several related vision tasks.
layout: 2 parts: left 5-column corruption grid, right legend and stacked task frames
description: The figure has two parts. On the left is a mosaic of five color-coded columns, titled Blur, Color, Noise, Quality and Weather, in blue, purple, teal, green and yellow. Each column has four frames from an animated forest scene, and each frame carries a corruption label such as Defocus, Contrast, Gaussian, JPEG, Fog or Rain. Small icons in the frame corners show whether the corruption is consistent in time (stopwatch), stereo (bowtie glasses) or depth (grid). On the right, a legend explains the three icons: Time, Stereo and Depth. Next to it, stacks of clean frames labeled RobustSpring, Optical flow, Scene flow and Stereo show the data and the tasks. The eye goes first to the colorful corruption grid.
caption: RobustSpring is a novel image corruption benchmark for optical flow, scene flow, and stereo. It evaluates 20 image corruptions including blurs, color changes, noises, quality degradations, and weather, applied to stereo video data from Spring. For comprehensive robustness evaluations, RobustSpring's image corruptions are integrated in time, stereo, and depth, where applicable.
abstract: Standard benchmarks for optical flow, scene flow, and stereo vision algorithms generally focus on model accuracy rather than robustness to image corruptions like noise or rain. Hence, the resilience of models to such real-world perturbations is largely unquantified. To address this, we present RobustSpring, a comprehensive dataset and benchmark for evaluating robustness to image corruptions for optical flow, scene flow, and stereo models. RobustSpring applies 20 different image corruptions, including noise, blur, color changes, quality degradations, and weather distortions, in a time-, stereo-, and depth-consistent manner to the high-resolution Spring dataset, creating a suite of 20,000 corrupted images that reflect challenging conditions. RobustSpring enables comparisons of model robustness via a new corruption robustness metric. Integration with the Spring benchmark enables two-axis evaluations of both accuracy and robustness. We benchmark a curated selection of initial models, observing that robustness varies widely by corruption type, and experimentally show that evaluations on RobustSpring indicate real-world robustness. RobustSpring is a new computer vision benchmark to treat robustness as a first-class citizen, fostering models that are accurate and resilient. It is available at https://spring-benchmark.org.
